nav.marketsLede: Every market we price, and what a month of per-capita income is there.

footer.tagline: What digital services actually cost, where you live, as a share of what people earn there.
footer.note: Every price carries a date and a link to the page it came from. Nothing is estimated. Where we could not verify a price, we say so.

method.title: Method
method.lede: One number, one formula, and a receipt for every claim.
method.formulaLede: ECI = local monthly price ÷ monthly per-capita income × 100
method.formulaNote: The answer reads as a share: an ECI of 1.5 means the subscription costs one and a half percent of a month of per-capita income.
method.denLede: GNI per capita, current local currency, from the World Bank — free, keyless, and covering every country with sixty years of history. Divided by twelve for a month.
method.denNote: This is an average per person, not a median wage. A median would be better but is not available free and comparable across every market. The number is therefore about the size of a typical share, not a typical salary.
method.priceLede: The price on the service's own page, in the market's own currency, read by a person and written down with a date.
method.priceNote: No price is published without a date and a link to the page it was read from. When a price is not verified it is not shown as a price.
method.watchLede: A nightly job fetches each pricing page and hashes it. When the hash changes, a person is told to go and re-read the price. The machine never writes a price.
method.coverageLede: How much of the database has been checked in the last 30 days.

home.title: The Real Local Cost
home.lede: Netflix is $15 in one country and the price of a week of groceries in the next. We price digital services in each market's own currency, then divide by what people earn there — so the number means the same thing everywhere.
home.flagTitle: The same subscription, in each market
home.flagLede: Each service's flagship plan as a share of monthly per-capita income. Lower is more affordable.
home.latestLede: Every price move we have verified, newest first.
home.methodLede: One number, one formula, no black box.
home.dataLede: The whole dataset, free, with sources. Use it, cite it, check it.

service.title: {service} prices, market by market
service.lede: The price of {service} in every market we track, and what that price costs as a share of what people earn there.
service.historyLede: Dated price points, each one read from the service's own pricing page.
service.noData: No verified prices for this service yet.

market.title: Digital subscriptions in {market}
market.lede: What each subscription costs in {market}, and what that costs as a share of what people earn here.
market.rankLede: What a month of each subscription eats out of a month of per-capita income.
market.incomeLede: The denominator behind every number on this page.

pair.title: {service} in {market}: {price}
pair.lede: {service} costs {price} in {market}. That is {share} of a month of per-capita income here.
pair.incomeHere: A month of per-capita income here is {income}.
pair.reference: In {ref} the same plan costs {refprice}. It takes {refshare} of a month's income there, against {here} here.
pair.historyLede: Every dated price we have verified for {service} in {market}.
pair.receiptLede: Where this price came from, and when we checked it.
pair.altLede: Local alternatives, and what they cost.
pair.howLede: The practical part: what is sold, where, and what it really costs.
pair.noPrice: We have not verified a {service} price for {market} yet.
pair.noPriceLede: We only publish what we can check against the service's own page. The markets we have verified are listed in the index.
pair.historyOnce: One price recorded so far. The chart fills in as more dated prices are verified.
pair.discontinuedLede: This plan is no longer offered here. The price shown is the last one we verified.

wire.title: The wire
wire.lede: Every verified price move, newest first. Each entry links the receipt.
wire.empty: No changes logged yet. The watcher runs nightly and writes here when a price page changes.

data.title: The data
data.lede: Everything on this site, as a file. Free, no sign-up, no key. Cite it, check it, build on it.
data.jsonLede: Every verified price with its history, verification date and receipt URL.
data.csvLede: The same rows, one per line, for a spreadsheet.
data.incomeLede: The denominator series, straight from the World Bank API.
data.schemaLede: The shape of the data, so you can join it to your own.
data.coverageLede: How much of the database was checked recently, and when.
